subject: A possible bug with transformed data

messages.author: 7d6a5c272d24acfa
messages.subject: A possible bug with transformed data
parts:
Hi all,

I encountered a possible bug in transformed data. I think stanc.exe is supposed to return an error in the following example.

A vector size should not be defined in the transformed data block, but stanc.exe does not return an error.

Here is my code to demonstrate:

transformed data
{ 
   // N and k[N] must be defined in data and N and k[1] and k[2] must be read from a file
   int N;
   real k[N];
   N <- 2;
   k[1] <- 4.0;
   k[2] <- 2.0;
}
parameters
{
   real<lower=0> lambda;
}
model
{
   for(i in 1:N)
   { 
      increment_log_prob(k[i]*log(lambda) - lambda);
   }
}

the error at runtime is:

Exception: INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=1; lower bound=1; upper bound=0; index position=1; k
Diagnostic information: 
Dynamic exception type: std::out_of_range
std::exception::what: INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=1; lower bound=1; upper bound=0; index position=1; k

Edit:typos are fixed.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] A possible bug with transformed data
parts:
This is not a bug, per se.  The problem is that N has not been given a value when k[N] is defined,
so k[N] is treated like a zero-dimensional array.  Move the declaration and setting of k[N] to the
transformed parameters block (or the model block if you don’t want those values saved).
